source: Analyst-derived annual INCIDENCE (new events per year, not prevalence). Anchored on the SELECT secondary-prevention rate and scaled by published relative-risk gradients across cardiometabolic risk states. A modelling assumption reconciling several literatures rather than an observed rate in this exact subgroup; swept in sensitivity analysis.

Annual INCIDENCE of type 2 diabetes among adults with obesity who do not already have it, derived from the placebo arms of the obesity pharmacotherapy trials that report progression from prediabetes — SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes recorded 6% of the placebo arm developing type 2 diabetes over 160 weeks. Scaled down for unselected obesity and up for the higher-risk subgroups. A modelling assumption.

Annual all-cause hospitalisation INCIDENCE, derived from published admission rates for adults with obesity and the comorbidity concerned. Used only to value the admissions an avoided event would have carried; a modelling assumption.

Annual INCIDENCE of newly diagnosed hypertension among adults with obesity who do not already have it, derived from cohort-reported incidence gradients by BMI. Subgroups that already carry hypertension have no row, because a condition already present cannot be newly incident.

Annual INCIDENCE of progression to moderate-severe obstructive sleep apnoea requiring escalated management. Derived from published apnoea-hypopnoea index trajectories with weight change; a modelling assumption.

SELECT (NCT03574597, Lincoff et al., N Engl J Med 2023): the placebo arm recorded a primary MACE incidence of 8.0% over a mean 39.8-month follow-up in adults with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease, which annualises to roughly 2.4% under a constant-hazard assumption. This is an INCIDENCE — new events per year — not a prevalence.
